notes: Endotext Non-Thyroidal Illness Syndrome was reread for the low-T3 pattern during severe illness and the progressive changes in T4/TSH with increasing severity.
Endotext Metabolism of Thyroid Hormone was reread for diminished D1-mediated T4-to-T3 conversion and impaired reverse-T3 deiodination/clearance, plus the contribution of transport and D3.
NCBI StatPearls Euthyroid Sick Syndrome was reread for critical-illness context, low T3 with low/normal T4 and TSH, cytokine effects and deiodinase changes.
The official USMLE 2026 Endocrine System page 31 was visually verified and explicitly lists nonthyroidal illness syndrome/euthyroid sick syndrome under thyroid disorders.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.early_pattern: Mild-to-moderate nonthyroidal illness commonly lowers serum T3 first; T4 may remain normal early and fall with more severe/prolonged illness.
claim_audit.d1_mechanism: Reduced hepatic/peripheral type 1 deiodinase activity diminishes T4-to-T3 conversion and reverse-T3 deiodination, contributing to low T3 and elevated reverse T3.
claim_audit.multifactorial_nuance: NTIS is multifactorial: altered transport, cytokines, hypothalamic-pituitary signaling, binding proteins and D3 can contribute, so the item does not claim D1 is the sole mechanism.
claim_audit.graves_distractor: TSH-receptor-stimulating antibodies cause Graves hyperthyroidism with elevated thyroid hormone and suppressed TSH.
claim_audit.thyroiditis_distractor: Destructive thyroiditis causes transient release of preformed hormone rather than the low-T3 metabolic adaptation shown.
claim_audit.rthb_distractor: THRB resistance produces high free thyroid hormones with inappropriately nonsuppressed TSH, not the low-T3 severe-illness pattern.
claim_audit.tbg_distractor: TBG elevation primarily changes total hormone levels and does not explain the critical-illness low-T3/high-rT3 physiology.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A critically ill patient without prior thyroid disease has low T3, preserved free T4, low-normal TSH and elevated reverse T3. This is the classic early nonthyroidal-illness pattern. Reduced D1-mediated T4-to-T3 conversion and reverse-T3 clearance is the most direct listed mechanism.
adversarial_second_pass.central_hypothyroidism_challenge: Central hypothyroidism can yield low/normal TSH and low thyroid hormones, but early NTIS commonly preserves T4 while T3 falls and reverse T3 rises; the sepsis context strongly favors altered peripheral metabolism.
adversarial_second_pass.reverse_t3_nuance: Reverse T3 is not a universally reliable diagnostic test in every clinical setting. It is used here as a mechanistic clue, not as a required clinical diagnostic assay or absolute discriminator.
adversarial_second_pass.medication_challenge: ICU drugs such as glucocorticoids, dopamine, propranolol or amiodarone can alter thyroid tests. None is specified, so the item tests the illness-associated physiology rather than a medication-specific mechanism.
adversarial_second_pass.protective_vs_maladaptive_challenge: Whether NTIS is purely adaptive or partly maladaptive and whether thyroid hormone treatment benefits selected patients remain debated. The item does not ask treatment or assert a universal adaptive purpose.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All options are plausible mechanisms of discordant thyroid tests and are parallel in level of detail.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No rT3 cutoff, T3 threshold, mortality estimate or fixed illness day is required.
